row.name: Via Convict Canyon and Bright Dot Lake
row.description: Follow the trail up from Convict Lake to Bright Dot Lake, then a use trail up the steep sand and gravel above it to the summit. About 13 miles round trip with roughly 5,000 ft of gain.

row.name: Cowardice
row.overview: Easier than neighboring Deception, which it resembles: technical climbing in the first two pitches, then extended snow broken up by small rock bands. Pitch 1 begins on the buttress that makes up the left wall of the couloir beside the one dividing Mount Morrison proper and Torre De Mierda; trend left into a shallow gully, passing rock steps to a 40' slab. This slab is the crux; thin cracks lead up it, and the rock is fragile (70m). Pitch 2 heads straight toward a rock headwall (70m). Next, work leftward through gullies and brief rock bands to a continuous couloir, around 160m from the base, with no rock steps, which reaches the Northwest Ridge.
row.approach: Take the Convict Lake trail and scree slope up into the hanging valley below the north face. The start is in the back corner of the northwest shoulder, between the north buttress and the subpeak Torre De Mierda, about 300 feet right of Deception and shared with Learning to Walk. The first pitch climbs the buttress on the left side of the couloir dividing Torre De Mierda from the main peak.
row.descent_text: The route ends on the Northwest Ridge. Either follow the ridge to the summit and descend the east face, or skip the summit: go down the ridge over loose third-class ground to a large open couloir on the north (skier's right) side, then descend very loose talus or snow.

row.name: Bloody Couloir
row.overview: Walking off is class 2: the Northeast ridge to a split, then the left slope straight down to the road above upper Laurel Lake. The ascent itself: snow reaching about 35 degrees lies under the couloir, which averages near 40 degrees. The steepest point, roughly 45 degrees and brief, is high up where the dividing rock finishes. When the angle eases to the ridge, go left to the summit.
row.approach: The couloir drops off the north side of Bloody Mountain and is visible from far away along the highway. Access is by Laurel Lakes Road, which leaves Sherwin Creek Road outside Mammoth; it is a rough road meant for 4WD vehicles or ATVs, and its upper end reaches Laurel Lakes beside the foot of the couloir. Without a suitable vehicle the road is walked, which makes for a much longer approach. A broad snow apron rises from the lakes to the start of the couloir, which is split by a central pillar into a broader, less steep left chute and a narrower, steeper right chute.

row.name: Via Fern Lake
row.description: Cross the San Joaquin River and take the Mammoth Trail and Beck Lakes Trail to Fern Lake, then climb scree to the ridge and the summit pyramid. About 7 miles each way, partly off-trail.

row.name: North Face
row.overview: The line of the peak's first ascent, climbed by Muir in 1872. It is a steep, exposed face where tiny holds are all there is, and Muir had a famous scare when he got stuck partway up.

row.name: Northeast Buttress
row.overview: Descent is via the Banner-Ritter notch, then a glissade to Lake Catherine. Decent stone on the technical parts. Reach the shoulder under the route over snow, starting from the Gem Lakes Trailhead past Thousand Island Lakes. The hardest moves are early, angling up and right. Higher, a corner system beside a big buttress gives way to loose, easy scrambling and then ledges leading to a wide face; go around a corner to the right as it steepens. Mostly 4th class.
row.approach: The approach from the Gem Lakes trailhead runs to the Thousand Island Lakes basin, which makes a good camp (mosquitoes can be thick in early summer). From camp, ascend the snowfield up to the shoulder under the climb and transition to the rock there; an ice axe is needed on the snow, and crampons if it is frozen hard.
row.descent_text: Head down toward the saddle separating Banner from Ritter, where both sides hold snow, so carry an ice axe. From the saddle, glissade the snow slope below it back toward the lakes.

row.name: Southeast Slopes from North Glacier Pass
row.description: Walk to Thousand Island Lake and North Glacier Pass, then up easy slopes. The hard part is picking the true summit among bumps.
